(a) Set-aside the order of taking cognizance dated:
09.07.12, inc.c.c.1161/12 passed by the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC,
Nelamangala, for the alleged offence punishable under section 143, 147, 448, 323,
506 r/w Sec 149 of IPC and consequently.

Quash the NC: 2024:KHC:10411 entire Charge Sheet in CC No.1161/12 on the Civil Judge (Jr.Dvn) and JMFC, Nelamangala,
for the alleged offence punishable under section 143, 147, 448, 323, 506 r/w Sec 149 of IPC.

(b) Pass such other relief/s as this Hon'ble Court deems in the facts and circumstances of the case,
in the interest of justice and equity.
2. Respondent No.2 submitted a first information to the Nelamangala Rural Police Station on 15.11.2011 on which basis Crime No.429/2011 has been registered for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 448, 323, , 506 read with Section 149 of IPC.

sentences.text: The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that the aforesaid complaint is a counterblast to the complaint to the FIR in Crime No.428/2011 lodged by the petitioner No.3 for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 504, 506 of IPC read with Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, which is now pending in C.C.No.185/2015 before the Additional Civil Judge (Jr. Dvn.), Nelamangala, Bengaluru Rural District.

His submission is that the marriage between respondent No.2 and petitioner No.2 has been resolved by way of a decree of divorce in M.C.No.1102/2011 dated 14.09.2012 which has attained finality, and thereafter, petitioner No.2 and NC: 2024:KHC:10411 respondent No.2 are leaving separately.

The offences which have been alleged in Crime No.429/2011 from which the above petition arises are that the petitioners came to the house of respondent No. 2, demanded certain amounts of money and threatened respondent No.2.
4.
Notice having ordered on respondent No.2, though served, respondent No.2 has chosen not to enter appearance.
Notice having been ordered to the counsel for respondent No.2 before the Trial Court the same is also being served, but none has entered appearance for respondent No.2.

5. A perusal of the documents indicates that there was indeed a complaint filed by petitioner No.2 in Crime No.428/2011 for the offences aforesaid on 15.11.2011 and it was only thereafter on the very same day that a complaint was filed by respondent No.2 which came to be registered in Crime No.429/2011.

It is clear from reading the said complaints that the complaint filed by NC:
2024:KHC:10411 respondent No.2 is a only a counterblast to the complaint filed by petitioner No.2.
6.
Be that as it may, a decree of divorce has been granted and petitioner No.2 and respondent No.2 are leaving separately.

Being of the opinion that the present complaint is a counterblast, I pass the following:
::ORDER::
i) The criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The complaint in Crime No.429/2011 registered by the Nelamangala Rural Police Station and the charge sheet laid in the said matter now pending in C.C.No.1161/2012 on the file of the Civil Judge (Junior Division) & JMFC, Nelamangala is hereby quashed.
Sd/-
